fixture_name: Cloverleaf-to-urban interchange conversion — INT preliminary design (Wikimedia PD geometry)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: A shortened collector-distributor weave carrying a recorded 1,100 pcu/h design-year peak flow is a substantive preliminary-design exposure (concentrated lane-change demand raising sideswipe/rear-end risk) correctly flagged before geometry is fixed in detailed design.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim is anchored to recorded input facts (retained reduced-length weave, 1,100 pcu/h) plus the verbatim EV-IN-015 checklist quote confirming junction-type-suitability and lane-balance/through-lane-continuity prompts, exceeding registry-citation-only.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed strictly as a PIARC-derived safety_concern audit action at the correct preliminary-design stage; no compliance/code conflation, and HSM Part C/IHSDM are invoked only as evaluation tools consistent with the INT baseline.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and staged: apply the cited checklist prompts now, quantify adequacy via HSM Part C interchange models or IHSDM, then conditional remedies (lengthen the weave or ramp-meter the entry) — actionable and viable at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are explicitly assessed and scoped out on the recorded basis that shared-use paths are grade-separated from the motorised weave; not applicable but duly acknowledged.

justifications.substance: Uncontrolled free-flow ramp-terminal crossings of retained shared-use paths directly conflict with the recorded corridor objective of improved pedestrian/cycle continuity and pose a genuine preliminary-design-stage safety gap.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (PIARC preliminary-design prompts requiring pedestrian/cyclist provision especially at junctions) is backed by the verbatim EV-IN-016 quote, with EV-IN-005 reinforcing all-user/thematic coverage, and layout/objective claims rest on recorded input facts stated in the scenario.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under the PIARC international baseline at preliminary-design stage, using checklist prompts as normative support without converting them into compliance findings or conflating categories.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable: names the Walkability Checklist/CQSI tools, prescribes controlled or grade-separated crossings at each path/ramp interface, and identifies the northern loop-ramp crossing for signalisation, all actionable at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are the explicit focus throughout—road_users, scenario, rationale, and recommendation all address their exposure at ramp terminals.
